state.note:
result   — the insight ran and reached a conclusion; `value` is present
           and shaped by the template
unknown  — the insight ran, looked, and reached no conclusion. A
           legitimate result, not a failure
no_result — there was nothing to run the insight against

reason.note:
Attached evidence, not part of the verdict. The result is `no_result`; the reason says why, underneath it. Closed set, defined in plans/00-MASTER-PLAN.md — a no result that none of the four describes is a finding for decisions/, not a fifth reason.
Only should_exist_not_found is adverse. The other three are gaps in our data or facts about the world and must never render as findings against the business.

coverage_ref.required: when reason == not_published; and when reason == not_held_or_unreachable AND the gap is standing
coverage_ref.note:
A result citing a coverage rule asserts a standing, structural fact about what we can get — this is what phase 3 needs to produce a no result from data rather than from an authored fixture.
not_held_or_unreachable has two origins and the citation separates them: WITH a coverage_ref it is a known, permanent gap in our holdings (a state whose registry we do not ingest); WITHOUT one, the acquisition attempt failed this time and may succeed next time. Same reason, different advice — "do not wait for this" versus "try again".

context_ref.type: reference to the derived applicant-context fact that decided it
context_ref.note:
not_required is not coverage. A sole proprietor has no registration to find anywhere — the reason is a fact about entity type and industry, not about a jurisdiction, so it resolves at assessment time from derived applicant context (decisions/004). Without the citation the reason is an assertion, and the F1 trace becomes authored, which plans/07-logic.md forbids.
Consequence carried deliberately: this reason can only be assigned on the second of the two passes (establish context, then interpret against it). On the first pass the insight knows only that it had nothing to work with.

evidence.note: What was consulted, including when nothing was found. Present and possibly empty on no_result — an empty evidence list is itself informative, and the analyst can see we looked.

sources.note: which sources answered, including whether default or opt-in

invariants: No field in any template may carry a judging adjective. No "high-risk", "suspicious", "poor", "good". If a value needs an adjective to mean anything, the adjective belongs to the assessment.
No template returns a grade, score or risk band.

There is no not-applicable state. Deciding an insight does not apply is a judgement and belongs to the assessment; the nearest honest insight-level statement is no_result with reason not_required — itself assigned from derived context, not by the insight in isolation.

templates.shape: agreement between something submitted and something found

source_refs: OBSERVED — review task `name` returns Verified / Similar Match / Unverified
confirmed.divergence:
The source's fourth value `unverified` is NOT in this enum. Confirmed that it means "nothing found to compare against": OBSERVED on records with formation=null and no registration. Under this model that is a no_result with a reason, or an unknown — not a verification outcome. The mapping every consumer must apply:
  unverified + no record to compare  → no_result (reason from coverage/context)
  unverified + record exists, no conclusion reached → unknown
Recorded rather than applied silently, because the source vocabulary is
what the API returns and the divergence is ours.

templates.shape: a measured quantity with a unit
templates.why_added:
Nothing in the previous set expressed a neutral number with a unit. Raised by two worked examples that the existing templates could not carry:
  - "the submitted address is 0.6 mi from the registration address" —
    computable today from addresses[].latitude / longitude and
    sources[].type: registration (OBSERVED)
  - "the domain was registered 14 days ago" against a formation date ten
    years old (doc 03, named as a fraud-investigator use case)
Not `count` (nothing is counted), not `status` (not an enumerated state),
not `classification` (no scheme).
constraints: The value carries no reading. 0.6 mi is ordinary for a business that moved suite and notable for one claiming a single fixed premises; which it is, is the assessment's call.
`of` is a checkable predicate, never a characterisation.

The unit is open by design. Distance between two addresses, age of a domain or a registration, time since a status change, a ratio between two counts — all are the same shape, and the flexibility is the point. A closed unit list would just be a taxonomy nobody asked for. What is closed is the shape: value, unit, what was measured, and between what.
templates.note: This is the template most likely to absorb work currently done by thresholded binaries. address_verification returns Verified / Unverified; the distance is the fact underneath that binary.

templates.shape: how many things match a predicate, with those things reachable

confirmed.status: SATISFIABLE TODAY, BUT NO REVIEW TASK DOES IT
confirmed.detail:
The distinction that matters: the template is not unsupported by the data, it is unused by the current check set.
Satisfiable now. The API returns addresses[], people[] and registrations[] as reachable lists with per-item attributes — OBSERVED: addresses carry labels (e.g. registered_agent), state, and sources[].type, and each item is individually addressable. So a count over a category predicate is computable from data already returned:
  - "2 of 4 addresses are registered-agent addresses"
  - "3 of 5 addresses are commercial and high frequency"
  - "1 of 2 registrations is outside the formation state"
The second of those is the interesting shape — counting attributes that fall
into a CATEGORY defined by more than one attribute. No check produces it
today; the concept does not exist yet, and the data supports it.
Not satisfiable from a band. location_frequency returns Low / Moderate /
High, documented as 1-20 / 21-100 / 101+ (doc 02), with no count and no list
of the businesses sharing the address. The signals surface gives a banded
range ("used by 21-100 other businesses", V802) — still a band.
rules:
Reachability is the constraint that keeps this honest and it is not negotiable. Dropping it would let "6 high-risk addresses found" back in through the door the model was built to close.
A banded value is a measurement whose value is withheld. Where only the band is available, record the band as `status` AND record the withheld value as a coverage limitation on that insight. Do not present a band as a count. If the underlying counts become reachable, location_frequency moves here.
`of` may compose several attributes ("commercial and high frequency") as long as each component is itself a reported fact. Composing facts is allowed; composing a judgement into the predicate is not.

set_decisions.why: Discovery asks whether a thing exists; verification asks whether what exists agrees with what was submitted. CONFIRMED against doc 03, which runs both: website_url_discovery (found / not_found) and then web_*_verification over what it found.

Status is an observed state in a source's vocabulary and carries no confidence. Classification always carries one. CONFIRMED: industry_classification has a confidence score; registration status does not.
A count is a cardinality with reachable items. A measurement is a quantity with a unit. Merging them would let a band masquerade as a count.
